title: Iraq's Army Enters Jurf al-Sakhar: Kataib Hezbollah, Oil Siphoning Claims and a Baghdad Deal
description_html:
Why has Iraq's army entered a stronghold the state stayed out of for about 12 years? Security forces moved into Jurf al-Sakhar, held by the Iran-aligned Kataib Hezbollah. We explain the leaked report alleging oil siphoning from state pipelines, the sacked Babil officials, the reported role of Quds Force commander Esmail Qaani, the one-month withdrawal compromise, and what it means for the US, Europe, the Gulf and India. Kataib Hezbollah denies the allegations.

Sources: Reports from Iraqi and regional media, Reuters, statements from Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, Iraq's Interior Ministry (leaked report as reported) and Kataib Hezbollah. Claims labelled as reported or alleged are not verified by us.
